B. TS = 0
C. ST = 1
D. ST - TS = 0
E. ST = T
F. ST = 0
G. ST = TS

2. Then, apply S to the result, which gives the derivative of xp(x), i.e., S(T(p(x))) = d/dx (xp(x)) = p(x) + xp'(x).

Notice that the result of S(T(p(x))) is not just p(x), but rather p(x) plus the product of x and the derivative of p(x). This means that S(T(p(x))) is not equal to p(x) itself.

Notice that the result of S(T(p(x))) is the same as the result of T(S(p(x))), which is p(x) plus the product of x and the derivative of p(x).

Since (ST)(p(x)) = p(x) + xp'(x) and (TS)(p(x)) = p(x) + xp'(x), we can conclude that:

(ST)(p(x)) = (TS)(p(x))

This means that ST = TS.
